draft.title: How rocks are used
card: A rock's properties include its hardness, how it breaks, how it feels and how well it lets water through. These come from how the rock formed.
People choose a rock for a job by matching its properties to what the job needs. A hard rock suits cutting and grinding. A rock that splits into flat sheets suits paving.

First Nations Australians chose particular stones for particular tasks. Coarse, hard sandstone was used for grindstones to crush seeds. Fine-grained stones that break into sharp edges were used for cutting tools.
This choice was made by knowing the stone well. It came from careful observation over a very long time and was passed on through generations.
draft.remember: Choose a rock for a job by matching its properties to what the job needs.

a.q: Why were hard, coarse stones chosen for grindstones?
opts: Their rough, hard surface can crush and grind seeds
Their soft surface wears away into a fine flour
Their smooth, glassy surface makes seeds slide off
Their light weight makes them easy to carry far
a.why: A grindstone must be hard enough to crush seeds and rough enough to grip them. A soft stone would wear away into the food. A smooth surface would not grind well.
a.clue: Think about what a grindstone must do to seeds.

b.q: A builder in Perth needs stone for a path that will be walked on daily and often get wet. Which property matters most for the choice?
opts: It is hard and wears away slowly under foot traffic
It is soft enough to be carved with bare hands
It is coloured to match the nearby garden plants
It is the same rock type as the stone in the house
b.why: A path is worn down by walking and weather, so a hard stone that wears slowly is the best match. A soft stone would wear away fast. Colour and rock type do not decide how well it does the job.
b.clue: Match the stone's property to what the job demands.

a.best: Their rough, hard surface can crush and grind seeds

b.best: It is hard and wears away slowly under foot traffic

People choose a rock for a job by matching its properties to what the job needs. A hard rock wears away slowly, so it suits cutting, grinding and surfaces that get heavy use. A rock that splits into flat sheets suits paving.

First Nations Australians chose particular stones for particular tasks. Coarse, hard sandstone was used for grindstones to crush seeds. Fine-grained stones that break into sharp edges were used for cutting tools.
This choice was made by knowing the stone well. It came from careful observation over a very long time and was passed on through generations.

a.q: A group needs a stone to grind seeds into flour. Which stone would suit this job best?
opts: A coarse, hard stone with a rough, gritty surface
A soft stone that crumbles easily when rubbed
A fine-grained stone that breaks into sharp edges
A light stone that lets water soak through it
a.why: A hard stone wears away slowly, and a coarse surface helps crush the seeds, so it suits grinding. A stone that breaks into sharp edges suits cutting tools rather than grinding. A soft stone would crumble into the food.
a.clue: Match the stone's properties to the work of grinding.
